drills.q: List the three triggers for a React component re-render, and explain why 'props changed' isn't a fourth independent one.
drills.a: Own state change (useState/useReducer), parent re-renders and the component isn't memoized, or a subscribed context value changes. A prop can only change because the parent re-rendered and passed a new value -- it's a description of what happens during trigger #2, not an independent cause.

drills.q: Explain mechanically why array index as key breaks state when a list is reordered.
drills.a: React matches list children across renders by key to decide whether to reuse a DOM node/component instance. With index as key, the key for 'whatever is now at position 0' is always 0 regardless of which logical item that is after reordering -- React reuses the existing DOM node (including uncontrolled state it holds) and silently reattaches it to the wrong logical item.

drills.q: Why must hooks be called unconditionally and in the same order on every render? What's the actual data structure behind this rule?
drills.a: React tracks each hook's state via its position in a linked list attached to the component's fiber, not by name -- there's no call-site identifier to match against. A conditionally skipped hook shifts every subsequent hook's position on that render, so React reads/writes the wrong stored state for all of them. Enforced primarily by the eslint-plugin-react-hooks rules-of-hooks lint rule.

drills.q: Trace this bug: setInterval inside useEffect(fn, []) calling setCount(count + 1) appears stuck alternating between two values instead of incrementing. Explain why, and give the fix.
drills.a: The effect runs once (empty deps), so the setInterval callback closes over count as it was during that one render (0). Every tick calls setCount(0 + 1), using the same stale captured 0 -- so it goes 0 to 1 then resets to 1 again forever, never incrementing further. Fix: use the functional updater form setCount(c => c + 1), which doesn't depend on the captured count at all.

drills.q: React.memo is applied to a child component but it still re-renders on every parent render. Diagnose and fix.
drills.a: memo does a shallow comparison of props; a new object/array/function reference every render (an inline literal, or an unmemoized inline callback) makes the comparison always see a difference even with identical contents. Fix: stabilize the reference with useMemo/useCallback at the source, or rely on the React Compiler if the component is eligible for auto-memoization.

drills.q: Describe a systematic method (not guessing) for diagnosing why a component re-renders unexpectedly.
drills.a: Open React DevTools Profiler, record the interaction, and use the 'why did this render' indicator to identify the specific trigger (props/state/hooks changed or parent re-rendered). If it's an unmemoized parent re-render with genuinely stable props, that's a real memo candidate. If props aren't stable, trace the reference instability to its source (usually an inline object/callback) rather than reaching for memo on the child first.

drills.q: Why is React's reconciliation algorithm O(n) rather than solving the general tree-diff problem (O(n^3))?
drills.a: React makes two heuristic simplifying assumptions: elements of different types at the same tree position are assumed to produce entirely different subtrees (so it just unmounts/remounts rather than diffing across a type change), and key is trusted as the developer-provided identity signal for list children instead of computing a true minimal-edit-distance match.

drills.q: What does the React Compiler do, since when has it been stable, and does it remove the need to follow the Rules of Hooks?
drills.a: It statically analyzes component code and automatically inserts memoization equivalent to hand-written useMemo/useCallback/React.memo. Stable 1.0 since October 2025, works back to React 17. It does NOT remove the need for the Rules of Hooks -- it depends on code following them (and other React rules) to safely analyze and transform it; violations can cause silent bailout to unoptimized behavior rather than an automatic fix.

drills.q: Why does putting all application state in one large top-level context tend to cause a re-render cascade as an app scales, and what are two architectural fixes?
drills.a: Any field update changes the context object's reference, and every consumer re-renders regardless of which specific field they actually read. Fixes: split the context into multiple narrower contexts by concern, or move high-frequency-changing shared state to a selector-based external store (Zustand/Jotai) that lets consumers subscribe to just the slice they read.

drills.q: Is index-as-key always wrong? Under what condition is it actually safe?
drills.a: No -- for a list that's genuinely static or only ever appended-to/replaced wholesale (never reordered, no mid-list insertion or deletion), index and identity coincide and there's no actual bug. The rule against index-as-key specifically applies to lists that can reorder, insert, or delete items.
